## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical NUMA-aware memory management, concurrency, and IO paths under contention. It requires precise state machines and race-free synchronization.

## Key Concepts

- NUMA-aware allocation
- per-page state machine NONE/PENDING/VALID
- CAS-based serialization to avoid duplicate fetch
- cross-node IO queues and read-ahead

## Code Example

```c
// Minimal sketch
typedef enum { NONE, PENDING, VALID } page_state_t;
struct page { atomic_int state; void *frame; int io_inflight; };
void handle_fault(struct page *p) { if (cas(&p->state, NONE, PENDING)) { enqueue_io(p); } else { wait_on_page(p); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test contention and ensure liveness?
- How to extend for write-back coherency and cache eviction?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests safe memory reclamation in shared-data paths, especially with per-core freelists and a global pool. It probes understanding of use-after-free scenarios, memory ordering guarantees, and the trade-offs between hazard pointers and epoch-based reclamation mechanisms.

- Hazard pointers

```
Block *blk = percore_freelist_pop();

lock(global_lock);
free_block(blk);
unlock(global_lock);
```
